\section*{Resumen de orientacion}
This document provides a practical system for evaluating, negotiating, accepting or rejecting job offers.

\section*{Contenido completo depurado}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Contenido completo depurado}




\subsection{Purpose}




This document provides a practical system for evaluating, negotiating, accepting or rejecting job offers.




It is designed for a Colombia-based Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist targeting international remote work, contractor/B2B roles, Unity WebGL, technical visualization, simulation, digital twin, XR-adjacent work and Python tooling as a secondary route.




The system is not legal, tax or immigration advice. Any contract, tax setup or relocation decision should be reviewed with qualified professionals.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{1. Core decision rule}




Do not accept an offer only because it is international.




An offer is strategically useful only if it satisfies most of these conditions:




\begin{enumerate}
\item compensation is above the minimum threshold;
\item net income is acceptable after taxes, fees and social security;
\item the role strengthens the real-time 3D / Unity / technical visualization path;
\item contract terms are clear;
\item payment risk is controlled;
\item IP and exclusivity terms are reasonable;
\item remote work from Colombia is legally and operationally feasible;
\item the role does not create major strategic dilution;
\item the work can build toward USD 3k–6k/month over 12–24 months.
\end{enumerate}




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\section{3. Offer scorecard}




Score each criterion from 1 to 5.




Then multiply by weight.




\subsection{Main scorecard}




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.305\linewidth}}
\toprule
Criterion & Weight & Score \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Criterion & Weight & Score \\
\midrule
\endhead
Gross compensation & 15 & 1–5 \\
Estimated net compensation & 15 & 1–5 \\
Role fit & 20 & 1–5 \\
Portfolio leverage & 15 & 1–5 \\
Contract clarity & 10 & 1–5 \\
Payment reliability & 10 & 1–5 \\
Remote feasibility & 10 & 1–5 \\
Growth / learning ROI & 5 & 1–5 \\
Total & 100 & — \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Interpretation}




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Total score & Decision \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Total score & Decision \\
\midrule
\endhead
85–100 & Strong accept / negotiate upward \\
70–84 & Acceptable if no hidden risks \\
55–69 & Renegotiate or accept only for cashflow \\
40–54 & Usually reject \\
Under 40 & Reject \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Automatic override}




Reject even if score is high if there is:




\begin{itemize}
\item no written contract;
\item unclear payment terms;
\item broad unpaid test;
\item abusive IP assignment;
\item illegal or impossible work authorization assumption;
\item non-payment history;
\item requirement to misrepresent status;
\item broad non-compete;
\item no clarity on contractor vs employee;
\item request for free production work.
\end{itemize}

\section{6. Gross-to-net checklist}




Before accepting a contractor offer, estimate:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule
Item & Question \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Item & Question \\
\midrule
\endhead
Gross monthly & What is the nominal amount? \\
Currency & USD, EUR, COP or other? \\
Payment fees & Wise, Payoneer, PayPal, SWIFT, bank spread? \\
Conversion loss & What exchange rate applies? \\
Taxes & What must be reserved? \\
Social security & EPS, pension, ARL? \\
Accountant & Monthly cost? \\
Software/equipment & Who pays? \\
Vacation & Unpaid or paid? \\
Sick days & Unpaid or paid? \\
Payment delay & 7, 15, 30, 45, 60 days? \\
Contract termination & How much notice? \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Net estimate formula}




Use a conservative model:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Estimated net = gross
- platform/payment fees
- currency conversion loss
- tax reserve
- social security
- accountant/admin costs
- unpaid time reserve
- software/equipment costs
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Required reserve}




For contractor income, keep reserves for:




\begin{itemize}
\item taxes;
\item social security;
\item slow payment;
\item contract termination;
\item equipment failure;
\item medical/emergency buffer;
\item unpaid vacation.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{EOR evaluation}




EOR is useful if:




\begin{itemize}
\item company wants employee relationship;
\item role is long-term;
\item compensation justifies EOR cost;
\item employer is willing to pay platform fees;
\item compliance matters.
\end{itemize}




EOR is less likely for:




\begin{itemize}
\item small studios;
\item short contracts;
\item low-budget roles;
\item trial projects.
\end{itemize}

\section{10. Take-home test evaluation}




\subsection{Acceptable test}




A take-home test is acceptable if:




\begin{itemize}
\item it is small;
\item it has a clear time limit;
\item it is relevant to the role;
\item it does not produce usable client work;
\item it has clear evaluation criteria;
\item it does not require unpaid multi-day labor;
\item IP terms are clear;
\item the company is credible.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Reasonable test examples}

\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}

\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Role & Reasonable test \\
\midrule
\endhead

Technical Artist & Shader/material or optimization task \\
WebGL & Small build/performance task \\
Tools & Small editor script \\
Python Automation & Small workflow script \\
Digital Twin & Conceptual architecture task \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Unreasonable test examples}




\begin{center}

\subsection{Test negotiation script}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I’m open to a focused technical exercise. To keep the scope reasonable, could we define an expected time limit and clarify whether the test is only for evaluation and not production use?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Test refusal script}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I’m not comfortable completing a large unpaid production-style task. I would be open to a smaller scoped exercise, a paid test, a portfolio walkthrough, or a live technical discussion instead.
\end{mdcode}

\section{11. Red flags}




\subsection{Critical red flags}




Reject or pause if:




\begin{itemize}
\item no written contract;
\item payment terms unclear;
\item company refuses to define scope;
\item asks for free production work;
\item broad non-compete;
\item broad IP claim over unrelated work;
\item payment only after client approval;
\item “remote” but requires unavailable work authorization;
\item asks to misrepresent legal status;
\item insists on employee-like control under contractor structure;
\item salary below minimum with no strategic upside;
\item company has public non-payment complaints.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Moderate red flags}




Negotiate or clarify if:




\begin{itemize}
\item vague role title;
\item unclear reporting structure;
\item unclear timezone expectations;
\item no onboarding process;
\item vague “startup equity” promises;
\item unclear tool/software reimbursement;
\item all communication only by chat;
\item no technical interviewer;
\item constant urgency;
\item trial period without clear compensation.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Low-level warning signs}




Monitor if:




\begin{itemize}
\item delayed recruiter responses;
\item overly broad job description;
\item role mixes too many unrelated skills;
\item no clear product/project;
\item old job posting;
\item compensation hidden until late;
\item vague remote policy.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{12. Offer-specific questions}




\subsection{Compensation}




Ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
What is the gross compensation?
What currency is used?
Is payment monthly, biweekly or milestone-based?
What are the payment terms?
Are there late-payment protections?

\subsection{Contractor structure}




Ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text

Is there a required platform?

\subsection{Scope}




Ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text

What does success look like?
What is the expected weekly availability?
How much meeting time is expected?
What timezone overlap is required?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{IP and confidentiality}




Ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Who owns the deliverables?
Does IP assignment apply only to paid work?
Are personal/portfolio projects excluded?
Can I show non-confidential work in my portfolio?
Are there confidentiality restrictions?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Technical role}




Ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text

What Unity version and render pipeline?
Is WebGL/XR/mobile/desktop the target?

\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{13. Acceptance thresholds}




\subsection{Strong accept}




Accept if:




\begin{itemize}
\item score above 80;
\item compensation meets target;
\item contract is clear;
\item role fit is strong;
\item remote structure is feasible;
\item payment risk is low;
\item no major red flags;
\item portfolio leverage is high.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Conditional accept}




Accept if:




\begin{itemize}
\item score 65–80;
\item compensation is acceptable;
\item role fit is useful;
\item risks can be negotiated;
\item cashflow or formal experience value is meaningful.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Reject}




Reject if:




\begin{itemize}
\item score below 55;
\item compensation below minimum;
\item role dilutes profile severely;
\item payment risk is high;
\item contract is unclear;
\item unpaid work is excessive;
\item authorization assumptions are false;
\item IP/exclusivity terms are abusive.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{14. Negotiation strategy}




\subsection{General rule}




Negotiate based on structure, not just salary.




Consider:




\begin{itemize}
\item rate;
\item hours;
\item payment timing;
\item trial period;
\item deliverables;
\item IP;
\item exclusivity;
\item scope;
\item timezone;
\item renewal terms;
\item portfolio usage;
\item software/equipment.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{If compensation is low but role is strong}




Negotiate:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
higher rate after trial;
shorter trial period;
reduced hours;
clear portfolio permission;
defined scope;
milestone payment;
review after 30/60 days.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{If role is good but contractor risk is high}




Negotiate:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
advance payment;
short payment cycle;
written contract;
clear termination notice;
paid test;
no broad exclusivity;
limited IP assignment.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{If company wants full-time contractor}




Clarify:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
expected hours;
exclusivity;
benefits;
paid time off;
tools;
whether relationship is truly contractor;
tax responsibility;
EOR possibility.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{15. Negotiation scripts}




\subsection{Ask for higher compensation}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Based on the scope, expected availability and the technical requirements around Unity, WebGL and real-time 3D visualization, I would be more comfortable at [target range].

If that is above the current budget, we could also discuss adjusting scope, hours, trial length or review timing.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Ask for paid test}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
I’m open to a technical evaluation. Since the task appears close to production work and may take several hours, would you be open to making it a paid test or reducing the scope to a shorter evaluation exercise?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Ask for clearer scope}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Before accepting, I would like to clarify the first deliverables, expected weekly availability, decision-making process and success criteria for the first 30 days.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Ask about IP}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Could you clarify whether IP assignment applies only to paid deliverables created under this contract, and whether my previous work, portfolio projects and independent tools are excluded?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Ask about contractor structure}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Since I am based in Colombia, I want to confirm whether this would be structured as an independent contractor/B2B agreement, EOR employment or another setup.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Decline politely}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Thank you for the offer. After reviewing the compensation, scope and contract structure, I do not think this is the right fit at this stage.

I appreciate the opportunity and would be open to reconnecting in the future if there is a role with clearer alignment around Unity, real-time 3D or technical visualization.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip

When comparing two offers, do not choose only by gross pay.

\subsection{Tie-breaker}




If two offers are similar, prefer the one that:




\begin{enumerate}
\item strengthens TwinSight-aligned positioning;
\item gives formal production experience;
\item has better payment reliability;
\item avoids legal ambiguity;
\item improves future compensation;
\item allows portfolio-safe work;
\item does not consume all time for low leverage.
\end{enumerate}

\section{18. EU mobility and offer evaluation}




\subsection{Current state}




Currently, evaluate offers as:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Colombia-based remote contractor
\end{mdcode}




Do not evaluate as:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
EU-authorized candidate
\end{mdcode}




until legal status exists.




\subsection{After Portuguese passport}




The offer pool changes.




Higher priority can shift toward:




\begin{itemize}
\item EU employee roles;
\item Germany/Portugal/Netherlands/Spain roles;
\item hybrid EU roles;
\item EOR or payroll roles in Europe;
\item stronger long-term compensation paths.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Germany route}




If German residence/work authorization becomes active, evaluate:




\begin{itemize}
\item German salary vs Colombian contractor net;
\item health insurance;
\item taxes;
\item cost of living;
\item local language;
\item career leverage;
\item long-term stability.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Do not relocate for weak offers}




Relocation should require:




\begin{itemize}
\item strong role fit;
\item legal clarity;
\item sufficient compensation;
\item housing feasibility;
\item health insurance clarity;
\item long-term career value.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{19. Role dilution test}




Before accepting, ask:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Will this role make my next application stronger for Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization?
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{If yes}




Likely strategic.




\subsection{If no}




Treat as cashflow only.




\subsection{If actively negative}




Reject unless survival requires it.

\section{20. Offer go/no-go checklist}




\subsection{Go}




Proceed if:




\begin{itemize}
\item role fit is clear;
\item compensation meets threshold;
\item net estimate works;
\item contract is written;
\item payment method is clear;
\item scope is defined;
\item IP terms are reasonable;
\item remote setup is feasible;
\item no false work authorization assumption;
\item no major red flags.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{No-go}




Do not proceed if:




\begin{itemize}
\item no written agreement;
\item payment terms are vague;
\item compensation below minimum;
\item unpaid work is excessive;
\item company refuses scope clarity;
\item IP terms capture unrelated work;
\item remote status is misleading;
\item requires unavailable EU/US authorization;
\item role damages the portfolio path;
\item company pressure feels manipulative.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\section{22. Final recommendation}




The safest decision model is:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Do not optimize only for the first paycheck.
Optimize for the intersection of compensation, contract safety and real-time 3D positioning.
\end{mdcode}




The ideal first international offer is not necessarily the highest gross number.




The best offer is the one that:




\begin{enumerate}
\item pays enough;
\item is legally and operationally clear;
\item strengthens the Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization path;
\item creates credible professional experience;
\item does not trap the profile in unrelated work;
\item can become a stepping stone toward USD 3k–6k/month.
\end{enumerate}
